# Table of tables

## Summary

GMNS 0.97 defines **25 resource files** grouped into four families: required, detail, signal-control, and dimension. Two tables (`link`, `node`) are required by the spec; the rest layer optional detail. This page is the "which table should I use?" entry point. For field-level detail (types, constraints, descriptions per column) see [Schema reference](spec.md).

The vendored 0.97 spec lives at `packages/netstead/netstead/spec/0.97/`. Each table is defined by a `<name>.schema.json` and listed as a resource in `datapackage.json`.

## Required

These two tables form the routable graph spine. A valid GMNS package must include both.

| Table | Purpose | Key foreign keys |
|---|---|---|
| `link` | Directed edges of the routable graph; one row per road segment between two intersections. Carries facility type, lane count, free-flow speed, allowed uses. | `from_node_id`, `to_node_id` → `node.node_id`; `geometry_id` → `geometry.geometry_id` (optional); `parent_link_id` → `link.link_id` (self-ref, optional) |
| `node` | Vertices of the routable graph; intersections, dead-ends, zone centroids. Carries x/y coordinates and control type. | `zone_id` → `zone.zone_id` (optional); `parent_node_id` → `node.node_id` (self-ref, optional) |

## Detail tables

Add geometric, lane-level, segment-level, or curb-level detail to the link/node spine. All optional.

| Table | Purpose | Key foreign keys |
|---|---|---|
| `lane` | One row per travel lane on a link. Carries lane number, width, allowed uses, turn restrictions. | `link_id` → `link.link_id` |
| `segment` | Sub-divides a link where attributes change mid-link (e.g., a lane drop). One row per segment. | `link_id` → `link.link_id`; `ref_node_id` → `node.node_id` |
| `segment_lane` | One row per lane within a segment. Same role as `lane` but at segment granularity. | `segment_id` → `segment.segment_id` |
| `link_tod` | Time-of-day override on link attributes (capacity, allowed uses) for a defined period. | `link_id` → `link.link_id`; `timeday_id` → `time_set_definitions.timeday_id` |
| `lane_tod` | Time-of-day override on lane attributes. | `lane_id` → `lane.lane_id`; `timeday_id` → `time_set_definitions.timeday_id` |
| `segment_tod` | Time-of-day override on segment attributes. | `segment_id` → `segment.segment_id`; `timeday_id` → `time_set_definitions.timeday_id` |
| `segment_lane_tod` | Time-of-day override on segment-lane attributes. | `segment_lane_id` → `segment_lane.segment_lane_id`; `timeday_id` → `time_set_definitions.timeday_id` |
| `movement` | A turning movement at a node, from an inbound link to an outbound link. Carries permitted uses and a movement type (left/through/right/u-turn). | `node_id` → `node.node_id`; `ib_link_id`, `ob_link_id` → `link.link_id` |
| `movement_tod` | Time-of-day override on movement attributes. | `mvmt_id` → `movement.mvmt_id`; `timeday_id` → `time_set_definitions.timeday_id`; `ib_link_id`, `ob_link_id` → `link.link_id` |
| `geometry` | WKT LineString per link. Referenced by `link.geometry_id`; optional (links can be implicit straight from-to). | (primary key; referenced by `link`) |
| `zone` | Traffic analysis zone (TAZ) polygons or centroids for demand modeling. | `super_zone` → `zone.zone_id` (self-ref, optional); referenced by `node.zone_id` |
| `location` | Curb-side point of interest — a stop, a pick-up location, a service door. | `link_id` → `link.link_id`; `ref_node_id` → `node.node_id` (`zone_id` is a plain column, not a declared FK) |
| `curb_seg` | A managed curb segment with allowed uses, parking regulations, loading-zone designations. | `link_id` → `link.link_id`; `ref_node_id` → `node.node_id` |

## Signal-control tables

Carry signalized-intersection timing and detection data. All optional; needed only when modeling signal operations.

| Table | Purpose | Key foreign keys |
|---|---|---|
| `signal_controller` | One row per signal controller (typically one per signalized intersection). | (primary key `controller_id`; no foreign keys — the controller is placed by the tables that reference it) |
| `signal_coordination` | Coordination relationships between controllers in a corridor. | `timing_plan_id` → `signal_timing_plan.timing_plan_id`; `controller_id`, `coord_contr_id` → `signal_controller.controller_id` |
| `signal_detector` | Detector loops / video zones on link approaches. | `controller_id` → `signal_controller.controller_id`; `link_id` → `link.link_id`; `ref_node_id` → `node.node_id` |
| `signal_phase_mvmt` | Maps movements to signal phases (which phase serves which turning movement). | `timing_phase_id` → `signal_timing_phase.timing_phase_id`; `mvmt_id` → `movement.mvmt_id`; `link_id` → `link.link_id` |
| `signal_timing_phase` | Per-phase timing parameters (min green, max green, yellow, all-red). | `timing_plan_id` → `signal_timing_plan.timing_plan_id` |
| `signal_timing_plan` | A named timing plan (cycle length, offset, plan identifier) for one controller. | `controller_id` → `signal_controller.controller_id`; `timeday_id` → `time_set_definitions.timeday_id` (when plan is TOD-bound) |

## Dimension tables

Vocabularies and configuration referenced by the detail and signal-control tables. All optional but typically present when any TOD or use-restriction is used.

| Table | Purpose | Key foreign keys |
|---|---|---|
| `time_set_definitions` | Named time periods (e.g., `weekday_am_peak` = Mon-Fri 07:00-09:00). Referenced by every `*_tod` table. | (primary key) |
| `use_definition` | A defined vehicle / mode class (auto, truck, transit, bike, walk). | (primary key `use`; named by `use_group.uses` and the `allowed_uses` columns, which are comma-separated text, not declared FKs) |
| `use_group` | A named set of `use_definition` members (e.g., `motorized` = {auto, truck, transit}). | (primary key `use_group`; members listed in its `uses` text field — no declared foreign key) |
| `config` | One row of network-wide configuration columns (`dataset_name`, length and speed units, `crs`, `geometry_field_format`, `currency`, `version_number`, `id_type`). | (no primary key, no foreign keys) |

## ER diagram

The core link / node / lane / link_tod / movement / geometry relationships:

```mermaid
erDiagram
    node ||--o{ link : "from_node_id"
    node ||--o{ link : "to_node_id"
    link ||--o{ lane : "link_id"
    link ||--o{ link_tod : "link_id"
    link }o--|| geometry : "geometry_id"
    lane ||--o{ lane_tod : "lane_id"
    node ||--o{ movement : "node_id"
    link ||--o{ movement : "ib_link_id"
    link ||--o{ movement : "ob_link_id"
    time_set_definitions ||--o{ link_tod : "timeday_id"
    time_set_definitions ||--o{ lane_tod : "timeday_id"
    zone ||--o{ node : "zone_id"
```

The signal, segment, and curb tables hang off `link` and `node` with the same shape but aren't shown here to keep the diagram readable. For the complete table list see the families above; for individual field detail see [Schema reference](spec.md).

## See also

* [Schema reference](spec.md) — auto-generated field-level reference per table.
* [What is GMNS?](../what-is-gmns.md) — design context for the spec.
* [Python tour (notebook)](../python-tour.md) — see several of these tables rendered in a notebook.
* [Glossary](glossary.md) — GMNS terms used above (TOD, segment, movement, …).


<!-- source: reference/glossary.md url: https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/netstead/reference/glossary.md -->

---
title: Glossary
audience: both
kind: reference
summary: GMNS-domain terms (link, lane, TOD, segment, …) and project conventions (sync state, scope, EditResult, Skill, MCP, …) defined in one place.
---

# Glossary

## Summary

Two sections: **GMNS domain** terms come from the spec itself and apply to any GMNS toolkit. **Project conventions** are Netstead + corral specific — names that appear in the API, CLI, and docs of this toolkit. Entries are alphabetical within each section.

## GMNS domain

**Allowed uses** — the set of uses permitted to traverse a link or lane (e.g., `auto, truck, transit`). Encoded as a comma-separated string on `link.allowed_uses` / `lane.allowed_uses` whose members name a `use_definition.use` or a `use_group.use_group` (a `use_group` row lists its members in its own comma-separated `uses` field). GMNS 0.97 has no `prohibited_uses` field. See [`use_definition`](table-of-tables.md#dimension-tables).

**Capacity** — the maximum hourly throughput of a link or lane under prevailing conditions, in vehicles per hour. Carried on `link.capacity` (and overridable per period via `link_tod.capacity`). Units are vehicles per hour per lane unless the producer notes otherwise; GMNS is silent on the LOS model used to compute it.

**Curb segment** — a managed length of curb (parking, loading zone, no-stopping). One row per curb segment in `curb_seg`, keyed to a `link_id`. New in recent GMNS versions; supports curb-management modeling.

**Facility type** — descriptor of a link's roadway class (e.g., `motorway`, `primary`, `tertiary`, `residential`, `service`). In GMNS 0.97 `link.facility_type` is free text — the spec does not enumerate it (`shared_categories.json` only defines `barrier`, `bike_facility`, `ped_facility`, `parking` categories, `movement_type` and `ctrl_type`). The quality rule pack reads it by name (e.g. `residential` for the high-speed-residential rule).

**Free speed** — the posted or signed speed limit, or the speed at which vehicles travel under uncongested conditions. Carried on `link.free_speed`; the unit is network-wide, declared in `config.speed` (usually `long_length` units per hour), not per link. Distinct from any modeled travel speed.

**Geometry** — a row in the optional `geometry` table holding a WKT LineString, referenced by `link.geometry_id`. When absent, the link is implicit straight-line from `from_node` to `to_node`. The geometry table exists so multiple links can share one shape (e.g., a divided highway represented as two opposing links sharing a centerline).

**GMNS** — General Modeling Network Specification. The Zephyr Foundation's open standard for routable transportation networks in tabular Frictionless Data Package form. See [What is GMNS?](../what-is-gmns.md).

**Lane** — a sub-element of a link with its own lane number, optional turn restrictions, and allowed uses. One row per travel lane per link in the `lane` table; `lane.lane_id` is the primary key and `lane.link_id` is the foreign key to `link.link_id`. A link with `lanes=3` typically has three corresponding `lane` rows.

**Link** — a directed edge in the routable network, from `from_node_id` to `to_node_id`. The required spine table; carries facility type, lanes, free speed, length, allowed uses. Undirected networks are represented by paired links (one per direction).

**Movement** — a turning movement at a node, from an inbound link to an outbound link. One row per allowed turn in the `movement` table; carries movement type (left/through/right/u-turn) and permitted uses. Used by signal-control tables to map phases to movements.

**Node** — a vertex in the routable network — intersection, dead-end, zone centroid. The required vertices table; carries x/y coordinates and optional `ctrl_type` (signal, stop, yield, no-control).

**Segment** — a sub-division of a link where attributes change mid-link (e.g., a lane drop, a facility-type change). One row per segment in the `segment` table; segments tile a link end-to-end. Used when link-level attributes are too coarse.

**Spec version** — the GMNS spec release the data conforms to. Netstead vendors 0.95, 0.96, and 0.97. Validation reports always include the spec version. The default is 0.97; override via `Network.from_source(path, spec_version="0.96")`.

**TOD (time-of-day)** — per-time-period overrides on link / lane / segment / movement attributes. Keyed by `timeday_id` into `time_set_definitions`. A period like `weekday_am_peak` (Mon-Fri 07:00-09:00) is defined once and referenced from every `*_tod` row that varies by that period.

**Zone** — a traffic analysis zone (TAZ) for demand modeling. Nodes carry an optional `zone_id`. The `zone` table holds polygon or centroid geometry; not every network has zones (routing-only networks often don't).

## Project conventions

**ApprovalRequired** — exception raised when a gated operation's cost estimate exceeds the approval threshold (default 180 seconds) and the caller has not set `approve=True`. See the cost-model section of [Architecture](https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/corral/architecture/#65-pooled-operations-cost-model).

**Auto-build threshold** — the network size (in nodes) above which a `netstead.scope` op logs an INFO message when it has to build the scipy graph index on first call (the build happens either way; the threshold only controls the log). Default 50,000 nodes. Configurable via the `NETSTEAD_AUTO_INDEX_THRESHOLD` environment variable. Pre-build explicitly with `net.build_indexes(graph=True)` to control timing.

**CORRAL_AUTO_APPROVE** — environment variable (`CORRAL_AUTO_APPROVE=1`) that bypasses the cost-model approval prompt for gated operations. Equivalent to CLI `--yes` or programmatic `approve=True`. Intended for batch / CI use.

**EditResult** — the value returned by every `netstead.clean` op. Carries the diff per affected table, the log entry for the operation, and a `_repr_html_` visual summary for notebook rendering. Integrated with `corral.editing.Session` for rollback.

**Engine** — the compute backend. corral has one: `IbisEngine` (lazy expressions over DuckDB). pandas / polars / pyarrow are I/O *formats* (`.to_pandas()` / `.to_polars()`), not compute engines. See `corral.engines`.

**NETSTEAD_AUTO_INDEX_THRESHOLD** — see *Auto-build threshold*.

**Lazy expression** — a `Table.expr` that has not been materialized. Operations on a lazy expression return a new lazy expression. Materialization happens explicitly via `.to_pandas()`, `.to_polars()`, `.collect()`, `.head()`, or `.count()`.

**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** — the open protocol Claude and other AI agents use to discover and call tools. Netstead ships an MCP server via `pip install 'netstead[mcp,graph]'`; start it with `netstead mcp serve`. Tools exposed: `describe_package`, `validate_package`, `list_tables`, `describe_network`, `quality_check`, `connected_components`, `scope_from_nodes` — all stateless, each taking a `source`. See the [MCP tools reference](../ai/mcp-tools.md) and [Architecture §6.9](https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/corral/architecture/#69-ai-accessibility).

**Network buffer** — a Dijkstra-bounded expansion in **graph distance** (using `link.length`). Used by `netstead.scope.from_node(id, network_buffer="200m")`. Distinct from spatial buffer.

**OutOfSyncWarning** — warning raised before `write()` or `validate(strict=True)` when any tracked foreign-key's source or target table hash has changed since the last validation. Indicates the in-memory FK graph may no longer match the data. Promote to an error with `strict=True`.

**Scope** — a `NetworkScope` is a (node_ids, link_ids) pair that, when applied via `.apply()`, returns a filtered `Network` with every other table pre-filtered by FK chain. Scopes are composable and chainable: `net.scope.from_nodes([1,2,3]).buffer_network("0.5mi").buffer_spatial(30)`. See [Architecture §6.2](https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/corral/architecture/#62-memory-efficient-scoping).

**Session** — `corral.editing.Session`, a context manager around one or more `EditResult`s with atomic rollback. Open with `with Session(net, log_path=...) as s: ...`; `s.rollback()` (no arguments) reverses every edit of the open session in LIFO order. The parquet log is written on clean exit only when `log_path=` is given; `corral.editing.rollback(pkg, log_path, to=session_id_or_datetime)` replays that log later to reverse edits selectively. (The Workbench's `netstead.workbench.Session` is a different class — the action bus of the local web app.)

**Severity / Category / Issue** — see the [corral API reference](https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/corral/reference/api/). `Severity` is one of `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO` (serialized lower-case). `Category` discriminates rule families: `SCHEMA`, `STRUCTURAL`, `FOREIGN_KEY`, `SYNC_STATE`, `DATA_QUALITY` — a quality finding carries `DATA_QUALITY` plus one of the three severities. `Issue` is the per-finding record carried in a `ValidationReport`.

**Skill (Claude Code Skill)** — a packaged set of instructions and prompts a Claude Code agent can load on demand. Netstead ships six (`gmns-author`, `gmns-build`, `gmns-validate`, `gmns-convert`, `gmns-clean`, `corral-validate`) under `skills/` in the repo. Install with `claude code skill add <git-url>#path=skills/<name>`. See [Architecture §6.9](https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/corral/architecture/#69-ai-accessibility).

**Spatial buffer** — a shapely-bounded expansion in **CRS units** (degrees for WGS84, meters for projected CRSs). Used by `netstead.scope.from_link(id, spatial_buffer_m=...)` and the `buffer_spatial()` chain method. Distinct from network buffer.

**Sync state** — content-hash tracking on every table via `DirtyTracker` (in `corral.validation.sync_state`). Records source + target hashes per FK at validation time so the validator can detect when a previously-checked FK has gone stale. Direct DataFrame mutations bypass the tracker — call `net.invalidate("link")` to force.

## See also

* [Table of tables](table-of-tables.md) — catalog of every GMNS resource referenced above.
* [Schema reference](spec.md) — field-level reference for the vendored spec.
* [Architecture](https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/corral/architecture/) — design rationale for the project-convention terms.


<!-- source: reference/settings.md url: https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/netstead/reference/settings.md -->

---
title: Settings reference
audience: both
kind: reference
summary: Every section and key of netstead.config.Settings — type, default, meaning — plus the file locations, precedence, env-var form and the secret-refusal rule.
---

# Settings reference

## Summary

`netstead.config.Settings` is the one model behind the Workbench's Settings dialog, the `netstead app` flags, `SetSetting` actions and the config files. It has twelve typed sections (`io`, `engine`, `osm`, `overture`, `build`, `validation`, `select`, `llm`, `assistant`, `viz`, `app`, `credentials`) plus a free-form `plugins` table. Every section rejects unknown keys (`extra="forbid"`), so a typo in a file is an error, not a silently ignored line.

The tables below are generated from the pydantic model: field names, types and defaults are the model's own. The "Applies" column says when a change takes effect in a running Workbench: **live** means the next action reads the new value; **next launch** means the server reads it only when `netstead app` starts (these four keys are tagged *applies on next launch* in the Settings dialog, and a session-scope change to them does nothing).

## Where settings come from

Precedence, lowest to highest — a later layer overrides the earlier ones key by key:

1. Model defaults (the tables below).
2. User file: `~/.config/netstead/config.toml` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/netstead/config.toml` when set; `%APPDATA%\netstead\config.toml` on Windows; `NETSTEAD_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the directory).
3. Project file: `./netstead.toml` in the current directory (or the `project_dir` passed to `load_settings` / `Session`).
4. Environment variables `NETSTEAD_<SECTION>__<FIELD>`.
5. Session overrides: CLI flags (`netstead app --port 9100`), `Session(overrides={...})`, and `SetSetting(scope="session")`.

`load_settings()` records which layer each leaf value came from; the Settings dialog shows that as a badge (`default`, `user`, `project`, `env`, `session`). Load the layers and read where a value came from:

```python
from netstead.config import get_value, load_settings

loaded = load_settings(environ={"NETSTEAD_VIZ__BASEMAP": "esri"}, overrides={"app.port": 9100})
print(loaded.settings.viz.basemap, loaded.sources["viz.basemap"])
print(get_value(loaded.settings, "app.port"), loaded.sources["app.port"])
print(loaded.sources["io.spec_version"])
```

Expected:

```text
esri env
9100 session
default
```

### Environment variables

The name is `NETSTEAD_` + the dotted key upper-cased with `__` for each dot: `NETSTEAD_APP__PORT=9100`, `NETSTEAD_LLM__OLLAMA__BASE_URL=http://gpu-box:11434`, `NETSTEAD_IO__ALLOWED_ROOTS='["/data/networks"]'`. A value starting with `[` or `{` is parsed as JSON (that is how lists and tables are passed); anything else is a string that pydantic coerces to the field's type. An env value outranks both files, and the Settings dialog says so when a saved value would not take effect.

### TOML files

Both files use the same shape — one table per section, nested tables for `llm.<provider>`, `llm.quality`, `validation.rules.<code>` and `plugins.<id>`:

```toml
# ./netstead.toml
[app]
port = 8900

[viz]
basemap = "esri"

[select]
provider = "ollama"

[llm.ollama]
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[validation.rules."quality.high_speed_residential"]
enabled = true
severity_override = "info"
thresholds = { max_free_speed = 45 }
```

`save_setting(key, value, scope="user" | "project")` writes one dotted key into the chosen file (and `value=None` removes it); the Workbench's **Save to** picker calls the same function.

### Secrets are never settings

API keys, tokens and passwords are refused everywhere settings are written:

* `SetSetting` refuses, before anything is recorded, a key or value that looks like an API key, a key whose last segment is secret-shaped (`*_key`, `token`, `password`, …), any URL carrying `user:password@`, and a `base_url` with a query string or fragment.
* `[plugins.<id>]` tables are free-form, so the model applies the same secret-name check to them in every layer — files and env included — and a hit fails validation with the key named, never the value.
* `llm.*` holds endpoints only; keys go through the Workbench's write-only key route or `netstead llm set-key` into the OS keyring. `credentials.keyring_hosts` names hosts, never what is stored for them.
* `io.allowed_roots` is config-only: the action API refuses to change it at any scope (a file, an env var or the command line can widen the sandbox; an action cannot).

## Sections

### `[io]` — reading and writing networks

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `io.spec_version` | `str` | `"0.97"` | GMNS spec version used to open networks and, unless a build names one, to build them. | live |
| `io.default_format` | `"csv" \| "parquet" \| "duckdb" \| "zip"` | `"parquet"` | Output format the Open / Import wizard prefills. | live |
| `io.allowed_roots` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Folders the Workbench may read and write (empty: the home directory). Config-only — see above. | live, config layers only |

### `[engine]` — DuckDB tuning

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `engine.threads` | `int \| None` | `None` | DuckDB thread count (`None`: DuckDB's own default). | not read yet |
| `engine.memory_limit` | `str \| None` | `None` | DuckDB memory limit string, e.g. `"4GB"`. | not read yet |

The Workbench notes this section as "not used yet: networks open with DuckDB's own defaults".

### `[osm]` — OpenStreetMap builds

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `osm.endpoint` | `str \| None` | `None` | Overpass API URL (`None`: the builder's default). | live |
| `osm.user_agent` | `str \| None` | `None` | User-Agent sent to Overpass / Nominatim (`None`: netstead's default). | live |
| `osm.timeout` | `int` | `180` | Per-request timeout in seconds. | live |
| `osm.retries` | `int` | `3` | Retries per request. | live |
| `osm.mapping_path` | `str \| None` | `None` | Path to a custom OSM-tag → GMNS mapping file. Declared in the model; no code reads it today. | not read yet |

### `[overture]` — Overture Maps builds

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `overture.release` | `str \| None` | `None` | Overture release string a build uses when the action does not name one (`None`: the builder's default). | live |
| `overture.data_root` | `str \| None` | `None` | Where Overture data is read from: a remote URL as is, or a local snapshot folder, which must lie inside `io.allowed_roots`. | live |

### `[build]` — Open / Import wizard defaults

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `build.network_type` | `list[str]` | `["roads"]` | Network types the wizard prefills: `roads`, `paths` or both. A single name is accepted; the old `drive` reads as `roads` and `walk`, `bike`, `all` as both. | live |
| `build.buffer_m` | `float` (> 0) | `1000.0` | Buffer in metres the wizard prefills for a point area. | live |
| `build.extra_tags` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Extra OSM tags the wizard prefills. | live |

### `[validation]` — quality rules

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `validation.rules` | `dict[str, RuleSettings]` | `{}` | One table per rule code (e.g. `quality.high_speed_residential`). | live (next validation) |

Each `RuleSettings` value has `enabled: bool = true`, `severity_override: "error" | "warning" | "info" | None = None` and `thresholds: dict = {}` (the rule's own threshold names). A code no installed rule has is reported as unknown by the validation result, not refused.

### `[select]` — natural-language selection

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `select.provider` | `"stub" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "ollama"` | `"stub"` | Which provider parses utterances (`stub` is the offline pattern parser). The old name `claude` is accepted and stored as `anthropic`. | live |
| `select.model` | `str \| None` | `None` | Model name (`None`: the provider's catalog default; for Ollama, an installed tool-capable model). | live |
| `select.grammar_first` | `bool` | `true` | Read a request with the offline pattern parser first and call the model only when that reading names a street, route number or road type the network doesn't have, or selects nothing. **Ask** does the same with the offline assistant (streets and columns must be in the network). `false` sends every request to the model. | live |

### `[llm]` — language-model endpoints and quality knobs

`llm.anthropic`, `llm.openai` and `llm.gemini` share one shape; `llm.ollama` has local defaults.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `llm.anthropic.base_url` | `str \| None` | `None` | Endpoint override (`None`: the official endpoint). Must be `http(s)`, no userinfo, query or fragment. | live |
| `llm.anthropic.timeout_s` | `float` (0 < x ≤ 600) | `60.0` | Whole-request timeout. | live |
| `llm.openai.base_url` | `str \| None` | `None` | As above (any OpenAI-compatible server). | live |
| `llm.openai.timeout_s` | `float` (0 < x ≤ 600) | `60.0` | As above. | live |
| `llm.gemini.base_url` | `str \| None` | `None` | As above. | live |
| `llm.gemini.timeout_s` | `float` (0 < x ≤ 600) | `60.0` | As above. | live |
| `llm.ollama.base_url` | `str \| None` | `"http://localhost:11434"` | The Ollama server. A non-local URL means utterances leave this machine. | live |
| `llm.ollama.timeout_s` | `float` (0 < x ≤ 600) | `120.0` | Whole-request timeout. | live |
| `llm.ollama.num_ctx` | `int` (2048 ≤ x ≤ 262144) | `16384` | Context window, in tokens, sent with every request. Ollama's own default (4,096 on recent versions) cuts off the assistant's prompt. Changing it reloads the model. | live |
| `llm.ollama.keep_alive` | `str` | `"30m"` | How long Ollama keeps the model loaded after a request (`"300s"`, `"1h"`; `"-1"` forever, `"0"` unloads at once). Ollama's own default is 5 minutes. | live |

`llm.quality` controls what the natural-language features send and how hard they try. `"auto"` means on for a local endpoint (Ollama, or any loopback `base_url`) and off for a remote provider.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `llm.quality.assistant_context` | `bool` | `true` | Send the shipped GMNS assistant notes (`gmns_assistant.md`) as context. | live |
| `llm.quality.assistant_context_max_chars` | `int` (0–100000) | `16000` | Cap on those notes. | live |
| `llm.quality.project_context` | `"auto" \| "on" \| "off"` | `"auto"` | Send the project's `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`. | live |
| `llm.quality.project_context_max_chars` | `int` (0–50000) | `4000` | Cap on the project notes. | live |
| `llm.quality.grounding` | `"auto" \| "on" \| "off"` | `"auto"` | Send network vocabulary (street names, route numbers) to the model. | live |
| `llm.quality.grounding_max_names` | `int` (1–2000) | `200` | How many names grounding sends. | live |
| `llm.quality.few_shot` | `bool` | `false` | Add this session's resolved selections as examples (same network only; never persisted). | live |
| `llm.quality.few_shot_max` | `int` (1–10) | `3` | How many examples. | live |
| `llm.quality.max_repairs` | `int` (0–5) | `1` | Re-prompts after an invalid tool call. | live |
| `llm.quality.temperature` | `float \| None` (0–2) | `0.0` | Sampling temperature (`None`: the provider's default). | live |
| `llm.quality.match_retry` | `"auto" \| "on" \| "off"` | `"auto"` | After a miss, re-prompt with only the closest real names (a bool is accepted: `true` → `on`). | live |
| `llm.quality.match_candidates` | `int` (1–20) | `5` | How many candidate names that retry sends. | live |

### `[assistant]` — the natural-language assistant

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assistant.actions` | `list[str]` | the 14 default action types (see below) | Core Actions the assistant may call. Opt-ins: `add_rows`, `set_setting`, `build_network`, `delete_selection`. `open_network` / `close_network` are never offered. | live |
| `assistant.plugins` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Plugin ids whose Actions it may call. | live |
| `assistant.max_steps` | `int` (1–20) | `6` | Tool calls per question. | live |
| `assistant.history_turns` | `int` (0–20) | `6` | Past turns sent with each question. | live |
| `assistant.max_turns` | `int` (1–500) | `50` | Turns kept in the conversation. | live |
| `assistant.output_token_limit` | `int` (128–8192) | `1024` | Output tokens per model call. | live |
| `assistant.context_max_chars` | `int` (1000–100000) | `12000` | Cap on the session state sent (grounded extras give way first). | live |
| `assistant.remote_token_budget` | `int` (0–10000000) | `200000` | Tokens a remote provider may spend this session before the assistant stops. | live |
| `assistant.compact_tools` | `"auto" \| "on" \| "off"` | `"auto"` | Offer a small model fewer tools per question (`auto`: on for a local endpoint). | live |

The default `assistant.actions` list is `select`, `clear_selection`, `pin_anchor`, `save_selection`, `use_selection`, `style`, `filter`, `navigate`, `set_active_network`, `run_validation`, `edit_cells`, `delete_rows`, `undo_edit`, `save_network` (`netstead.config.DEFAULT_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS`). It uses `select.provider` / `select.model` and the `llm.quality` privacy gates.

### `[viz]` — map rendering

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `viz.basemap` | `"positron" \| "esri"` | `"positron"` | Basemap style; a change applies without reloading the page. | live |

### `[app]` — the Workbench web server

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app.host` | `str` | `"127.0.0.1"` | Bind address. A non-loopback host prints a warning at launch. | next launch |
| `app.port` | `int` | `8850` | TCP port. | next launch |
| `app.console` | `bool` | `false` | Tagged as a launch-time key in the Settings dialog; no code reads it today. | next launch |
| `app.approve_above_s` | `float` (≥ 0) | `90.0` | A build estimated to take longer than this (or that cannot be estimated) needs `approved=True`. | live |
| `app.disabled_plugins` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Plugin ids not to load. | next launch |

### `[credentials]` — host names only

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `credentials.keyring_hosts` | `list[str]` | `[]` | Hosts whose secrets live in the OS keyring (names only). The Workbench notes this section as not used yet. | not read yet |

### `[plugins.<id>]` — per-plugin tables

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins` | `dict[str, dict]` | `{}` | One free-form table per Workbench plugin id, validated by that plugin's own settings model when it installs. Secret-named keys are refused in every layer. | per plugin |

For example, the bundled project-cards plugin reads `[plugins.project_cards]`:

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.project_cards.catalog_dir` | `str \| None` | `None` | A folder of ProjectCard files to open as the Cards panel's catalog on load (equivalent to calling `project_cards.open_catalog` once at startup). Must resolve inside `io.allowed_roots`. | next open |
| `plugins.project_cards.enable_apply` | `bool` | `false` | Turn on applying catalog cards to a network (`project_cards.apply_card` and the Cards panel's **Apply…**). Off, `apply_card` is refused and the panel offers no Apply. The assistant is never offered `apply_card`. | live |

## See also

* [Explore in the Workbench](../cookbook/workbench.md#settings) — the Settings dialog, scopes and badges.
* [Write a Workbench plugin](../cookbook/workbench-plugins.md) — how a plugin declares its `[plugins.<id>]` model.
* [Local language models (Ollama)](../cookbook/local-llm-ollama.md) — the `select` / `llm` keys in practice.

<!-- source: reference/workbench-actions.md url: https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/netstead/reference/workbench-actions.md -->

---
title: Workbench Actions reference
audience: both
kind: reference
summary: The 21 core Workbench Actions — fields, defaults, whether each mutates or runs as a job, and the replay snippet form — plus how to dispatch them from Python.
---

# Workbench Actions reference

## Summary

Every state change in a Workbench session — a click in the browser, a line of Python, a step the assistant drafts — is one typed Action: a pydantic model in `netstead.workbench.actions`, discriminated on its `type` string. The session validates the Action, applies it under its lock, records a `HistoryEntry` and publishes the new state. Because the vocabulary is the same everywhere, anything the UI did can be copied as Python and replayed.

This page lists the 21 core Actions in `netstead.workbench.actions.CORE_ACTIONS` (plugins register more). For each: the fields with their types and defaults (a field with no default is required), the class flags, and the snippet `to_python` writes for it. The flags are class attributes:

* **mutates** — the assistant must draft the Action and get approval before applying it; it also marks what `undo` and rollback care about.
* **runs as job** — the slow work runs on a background job thread; `Session.dispatch` waits for it, `Session.submit` returns the `Job`.
* **replay** — what the "copy as Python" snippet does with the fields: fields equal to their default are omitted; `replay_omits` fields are left out (`expected_version`, a guard that only means something in the live session); `replay_overrides` are forced (`BuildNetwork` always replays with `approved=True`).

All 21 core Actions have `assistant = True`, the class flag that lets an Action be offered to the natural-language assistant at all. The flag matters for plugin Actions: a plugin that is opted in through `assistant.plugins` can still keep one of its Actions out of the assistant's tools by setting `assistant = False` on that class. Which *core* Actions the assistant may call is a setting, `assistant.actions` (14 by default; `open_network` and `close_network` are never offered) — see the [Settings reference](settings.md#assistant-the-natural-language-assistant).

## Actions

### Open, close, switch

#### `OpenNetwork` — `open_network`

Load a GMNS network from a local path (inside `io.allowed_roots`) or URL and make it active. Runs as a job (`open <name>`); does not mutate. Result: `{"net_id": ...}`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `str` | required |
| `label` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` (derived from the source) |

Replay: `app.do(OpenNetwork(source='/data/net', label='Leavenworth'))`

#### `CloseNetwork` — `close_network`

Close an open network. Mutates (it throws away unsaved edits).

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str` | required |

Replay: `app.do(CloseNetwork(net_id='leavenworth'))`

#### `SetActiveNetwork` — `set_active_network`

Switch which open network the map and tables show.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str` | required |

Replay: `app.do(SetActiveNetwork(net_id='leavenworth'))`

### Select, pin, save, use, delete selection

#### `Select` — `select`

Select features by natural-language utterance or explicit ids. Give exactly one of `utterance` or `link_ids`. `query` is the parsed intent for `utterance` (the selection tool's arguments); with it no parser runs, so a replay is exact — the assistant records its selections this way.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` (the active network) |
| `component` | `"roadway" \| "transit"` | `"roadway"` |
| `utterance` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `link_ids` | `list[int \| str] \| None` | `None` |
| `query` | `dict \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(Select(link_ids=[1, 2, 3]))` or `app.do(Select(utterance='Ski Hill Drive'))`

#### `ClearSelection` — `clear_selection`

Clear the current selection. No fields.

Replay: `app.do(ClearSelection())`

#### `PinAnchor` — `pin_anchor`

Pin the current selection's `from` or `to` anchor to one node, then resolve the selection again (`node_id=None` unpins). A pin that resolves nothing is refused.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | `"from" \| "to"` | required |
| `node_id` | `int \| str \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(PinAnchor(role='to', node_id=60))`

#### `SaveSelection` — `save_selection`

Save the current selection under `name` (refused if the name is taken). Names: letters, digits, space, `_ . -`, up to 64 characters.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |

Replay: `app.do(SaveSelection(name='ski hill'))`

#### `UseSelection` — `use_selection`

Make a saved selection current again, resolved against its network as it is now.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |

Replay: `app.do(UseSelection(name='ski hill'))`

#### `DeleteSelection` — `delete_selection`

Forget a saved selection. Mutates (it throws away something the user made, so the assistant drafts it).

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |

Replay: `app.do(DeleteSelection(name='ski hill'))`

### Style, filter, navigate

#### `Style` — `style`

Partially update the map style; omitted fields are unchanged. `color_by` colors links by a column of the link
table and `node_color_by` colors nodes by one of the node table (`"none"` for a single color); `width_by`
sizes links by a numeric column (`"none"` for widths by lane count). A fresh session defaults `color_by` to
`"facility_type"` and `node_color_by` to `"ctrl_type"` when those columns exist (`"none"` otherwise).

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `color_by` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `node_color_by` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `width_by` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `ramp` | `"YlOrRd" \| "Blues" \| "Viridis" \| None` | `None` |
| `show` | `dict[("links" \| "nodes" \| "labels" \| "selection"), bool] \| None` | `None` |
| `colors` | `dict[("links" \| "nodes" \| "selection"), [r, g, b]] \| None` | `None` |
| `offset` | `bool \| None` | `None` |
| `show_direction` | `bool \| None` | `None` |
| `show_legend` | `bool \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(Style(width_by='lanes'))`

#### `Filter` — `filter`

Show only the links matching every condition; the map dims the rest and the table's Filtered scope lists them. A constrained predicate over link columns, never SQL. `where=None` (or an empty list) clears the filter; at most `MAX_FILTER_CONDITIONS` conditions.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `where` | `list[FilterCond] \| None` | `None` |

A `FilterCond` is `{col: str, op: FilterOp, val}` with `op` one of `eq ne lt lte gt gte in contains isnull notnull any_of all_of none_of between`; `in` takes a list, `isnull` / `notnull` take no value. The token operators `any_of` / `all_of` / `none_of` match a list of values against a comma-separated cell such as `allowed_uses` (`"auto"` matches `"auto,truck,walk"`; a bare value is read as a one-element list; an empty cell matches only `none_of`). `between` takes `[low, high]`, inclusive.

Replay: `app.do(Filter(where=[{'col': 'lanes', 'op': 'gte', 'val': 2}]))`

#### `Navigate` — `navigate`

Move the map camera. Give exactly one of `bbox`, `to_network`, `to_selection`, `record`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `bbox` | `(west, south, east, north) \| None` | `None` |
| `to_network` | `bool` | `False` |
| `to_selection` | `bool` | `False` |
| `record` | `RecordRef \| None` | `None` |

A `RecordRef` is `{table: "link" | "node", id: int | str}`.

Replay: `app.do(Navigate(to_selection=True))` or `app.do(Navigate(record={'table': 'link', 'id': 170}))`

### Validation

#### `RunValidation` — `run_validation`

Validate a network — spec, keys, structure, and the quality rules configured in `validation.rules` — as a job (`validate <network>`). Does not mutate. Result: `{net_id, version, stale, superseded, counts: {error, warning, info}, unknown_rules}`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `quality` | `bool` | `True` |

Replay: `app.do(RunValidation())`

### Edit cells, delete rows, add rows, undo, save

#### `EditCells` — `edit_cells`

Set cells on rows of one table, picked by primary key (`None` clears a cell). Values are coerced to the column's storage type; key columns and unknown columns are refused. Spec problems with the new values come back as warnings, never blocks. Mutates. Replay omits `expected_version`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `component` | `"roadway" \| "transit"` | `"roadway"` |
| `table` | `str` | `"link"` |
| `ids` | `list[int \| str]` (1–10 000) | required |
| `values` | `dict[str, bool \| int \| float \| str \| None]` (≥ 1) | required |
| `note` | `str \| None` (≤ 500) | `None` |
| `expected_version` | `int \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(EditCells(ids=[170], values={'lanes': 2}))`

#### `DeleteRows` — `delete_rows`

Delete rows of one table by key, with every row that depends on them through the spec's foreign keys (a link takes its lanes and time-of-day rows; a node a link still uses is refused). Mutates. Replay omits `expected_version`, so a replayed delete plans again against the network it runs on.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `component` | `"roadway" \| "transit"` | `"roadway"` |
| `table` | `str` | `"link"` |
| `ids` | `list[int \| str]` (1–10 000) | required |
| `note` | `str \| None` (≤ 500) | `None` |
| `expected_version` | `int \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(DeleteRows(ids=[170]))`

#### `AddRows` — `add_rows`

Append rows to one table (Python and the API only; the app has no drawing tool). Each row needs its key. Mutates.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `component` | `"roadway" \| "transit"` | `"roadway"` |
| `table` | `str` | required |
| `rows` | `list[dict[str, bool \| int \| float \| str \| None]]` (1–10 000) | required |
| `note` | `str \| None` (≤ 500) | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(AddRows(table='node', rows=[{'node_id': 900, 'x_coord': -120.66, 'y_coord': 47.6}]))`

#### `UndoEdit` — `undo_edit`

Revert the network's last edit, when the Workbench made it (a plugin undoes its own changes). Mutates.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(UndoEdit())`

#### `RedoEdit` — `redo_edit`

Re-apply the network's newest undone edit (the one `undo_edit` took back most recently). Any other change to
the network since the undo makes it unavailable, and it is refused with "nothing to redo" when there is
nothing to redo. Mutates.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |

Replay: `app.do(RedoEdit())`

#### `SaveNetwork` — `save_network`

Write the open network, with its edits, as a new copy in `output_dir`; the source is never written to and the copy never overwrites anything. Refused while the network has open edit warnings unless `accept_warnings`. Mutates; runs as a job (`save <name>`). A replayed save writes the copy again, so it fails with "already exists" while the earlier copy is there.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `net_id` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `output_dir` | `str` | required |
| `output_format` | `"parquet" \| "csv" \| "duckdb" \| "zip"` | required |
| `name` | `str` (file-name characters, ≤ 100; a format suffix must match `output_format`) | required |
| `accept_warnings` | `bool` | `False` |

Replay: `app.do(SaveNetwork(output_dir='/data/out', output_format='parquet', name='leavenworth-edited'))`

### Build

#### `BuildNetwork` — `build_network`

Build a GMNS network from OSM or Overture, write it to `output_dir`, then open it from disk. Give exactly one of `area` (fetch from the service) or `input_file` (a local `.osm` / Overpass `.json`, or an Overture snapshot folder). Without `approved`, a build estimated over `app.approve_above_s` (or that cannot be estimated) fails with `ApprovalRequired`. Mutates; runs as a job (`build <name>`); replay forces `approved=True`.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | `"osm" \| "overture"` | required |
| `area` | `BboxArea \| PointArea \| PlaceArea \| None` (discriminated on `kind`) | `None` |
| `input_file` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `output_dir` | `str` | required |
| `output_format` | `"parquet" \| "csv" \| "duckdb" \| "zip"` | required |
| `name` | `str` (file-name characters, ≤ 100) | required |
| `network_types` | `list[str]` (one or more of `roads`, `paths`; kept if any allows it) | `["roads"]` (a recorded single `network_type` is still read; recorded `drive` replays as `roads`, and `walk`, `bike`, `all` as `roads` + `paths`) |
| `extra_tags` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` |
| `spec_version` | `str \| None` | `None` (`io.spec_version`) |
| `overture_release` | `str \| None` | `None` (`overture.release`; only with `source="overture"`) |
| `label` | `str \| None` | `None` |
| `approved` | `bool` | `False` |

Replay: `app.do(BuildNetwork(source='osm', area={'kind': 'bbox', 'bbox': (-78.91, 35.98, -78.88, 36.01)}, output_dir='/data/out', output_format='parquet', name='durham-core', approved=True))`

### Set setting

#### `SetSetting` — `set_setting`

Change a setting (dotted key) for this session, or persist it to the user or project file. Refuses API-key-shaped keys and values at validation, before anything is recorded; `io.allowed_roots` is refused by the session at every scope. Mutates.

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `str` | required |
| `value` | `Any` | `None` (removes the key from that scope) |
| `scope` | `"session" \| "user" \| "project"` | `"session"` |

Replay: `app.do(SetSetting(key='viz.basemap', value='esri'))`

## From Python

`netstead.workbench.Session` is the action bus. Construct one (it loads settings from the usual layers; `overrides` is the session layer), dispatch Actions with `session.dispatch(...)` — `session.do` is the same method, which is why copied snippets read `app.do(...)` — and read `session.history`, a list of `HistoryEntry` records each carrying the Action as JSON, its `python` replay snippet, `ok`, `result` and any `error`.

The fixture folder is passed as an allowed root because a `Session` built from Python only trusts the folders in `io.allowed_roots`:

```python
from netstead.fixtures import leavenworth
from netstead.workbench import Filter, OpenNetwork, Select, Session, Style

source = str(leavenworth.csv_dir())
app = Session(overrides={"io.allowed_roots": [source]})

print(app.do(OpenNetwork(source=source, label="Leavenworth")))
selection = app.do(Select(link_ids=[1, 2, 3]))
print(selection["status"], selection["link_ids"])
app.do(Style(width_by="lanes"))
app.do(Filter(where=[{"col": "lanes", "op": "gte", "val": 2}]))

for entry in app.history:
    print(entry.seq, entry.ok, entry.python)
```

Expected:

```text
{'net_id': 'leavenworth'}
resolved [1, 2, 3]
1 True app.do(OpenNetwork(source='...
2 True app.do(Select(link_ids=[1, 2, 3]))
3 True app.do(Style(width_by='lanes'))
4 True app.do(Filter(where=[{'col': 'lanes', 'op': 'gte', 'val': 2}]))
```

Three details worth knowing:

* `dispatch` raises the recorded failure's type — `ApprovalRequired` (with `.estimate`), `PathNotAllowed`, `NotSupportedYet`, `JobCancelled`, else `ActionError`. `dispatch_recorded` returns the `HistoryEntry` instead and never raises `ActionError`.
* A `dict` is accepted in place of a model: `app.do({"type": "style", "width_by": "lanes"})` is parsed through the session's registry (`session.actions`), which also knows plugin Actions. `netstead.workbench.actions.parse_action` parses core Actions only.
* `Session.add_network(net)` registers an already-loaded `Network` without an Action, so it is not in the history and a copied script does not replay it.

## See also

* [Explore in the Workbench](../cookbook/workbench.md) — the same Actions from the browser, and "Every action is replayable".
* [Write a Workbench plugin](../cookbook/workbench-plugins.md) — registering plugin Actions on the same bus.
* [Settings reference](settings.md) — `assistant.actions`, `app.approve_above_s`, `io.allowed_roots`.
* [API reference](api.md#workbench) — `Session`, `BaseAction`, `CORE_ACTIONS`, `to_python`.


<!-- source: reference/workbench-http-api.md url: https://e-lo.github.io/netstead/netstead/reference/workbench-http-api.md -->

---
title: Workbench HTTP API reference
audience: both
kind: reference
summary: Every route the Workbench server exposes, grouped by area, generated from its OpenAPI document at build time.
---

# Workbench HTTP API reference

## Summary

`netstead app` serves one Workbench `Session` as a local web app. The browser front end is only a
client of the routes below; anything it does, a script can do with `curl` or an HTTP library. The
route list is generated on every docs build from the FastAPI app's OpenAPI document
(`build_app(session).openapi()`), so it cannot drift from the code; a running server serves the same
document at `/openapi.json` and interactive docs at `/docs`.

Every state change goes through one route, `POST /api/actions`, whose body is one Action (a JSON
object discriminated on its `type`). The Action schemas are on the
[Workbench Actions](workbench-actions.md) page; `GET /api/actions` returns the JSON schema of every
Action the running session accepts, plugin Actions included. Reads are plain `GET`s and never
recorded in the history.

### Events (`GET /api/events`)

The stream is Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`). It opens with a `state` event carrying the
full session snapshot (the same payload as `GET /api/state`) and then carries every event the
session publishes, each frame named by its `type`:

- `state` — a fresh snapshot after any change (open, close, selection, settings, edits).
- `history` — one recorded Action, in the shape `GET /api/history` lists.
- `job` — a background job's snapshot at each stage change (open, build, validate, save and Ollama
  pulls run as jobs; `POST /api/actions` answers `202` with the job and the outcome arrives here).
- `llm` — provider and key status after a key is set or removed or a model pulled.
- `navigate` — a map navigation request raised by a `Navigate` Action.

A `: keepalive` comment is sent after 15 seconds of silence so proxies keep the connection open;
`?max_events=N` closes the stream after `N` events, for scripts and tests.

### Local-bind guards

On the default loopback bind the server answers `400` to any request whose `Host` header is not
`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and `403` to any state-changing request that names a foreign
`Origin` or arrives `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`; see
[Explore in the Workbench](../cookbook/workbench.md#quick-start) for what that means when you
expose the app.

### Plugin routes

Each installed plugin's router is mounted under `/api/plugins/<id>/` and its static files under
`/plugins/<id>/`. Those routes depend on what is installed, so they are not listed here;
`GET /api/plugins` names the installed plugins and their state.

## Routes

{% raw %}
### Session

The session as a whole: its state, settings, history and the Action bus.

#### `GET /api/state`

Responses: `200` Successful Response

#### `GET /api/config`

Responses: `200` Successful Response

#### `GET /api/settings`

Responses: `200` Successful Response

#### `GET /api/history`

Every entry, plus the import lines that head them as a script ("copy session as Python").

A nested entry (``parent_seq`` set) is written as a comment, since replaying its parent repeats
it, so it needs no import.

Responses: `200` Successful Response

#### `GET /api/actions`

Every Action this session accepts, with its owner and JSON schema. Read-only; nothing is recorded.

Responses: `200` Successful Response

#### `POST /api/actions`

Apply an action. A job action (open/build) answers 202 with its job; the outcome arrives over SSE.

Request body: a JSON object (free-form; see the description).

Responses: `200` Successful Response · `422` Validation Error

#### `GET /api/events`

SSE stream: a ``state`` snapshot first, then every published event.

``max_events`` closes the stream after that many events (tests and scripted clients).

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_events` | query | integer or null | no |  |

Responses: `200` Successful Response · `422` Validation Error

### Jobs

Background jobs started by job Actions (open, build, validate, save) and by Ollama pulls.

#### `GET /api/jobs`

Every background job this session started, newest first.

### Selection

#### `GET /api/selection/export`

The current (or the saved ``name``) selection as a fragment or ProjectCard object, with a file name.

``form`` is the Find tab's ``segment`` (facility name + from/to) or ``link_list`` (only the ids), written
in ``id_system`` (``gmns``, ``osm`` or ``gers``); ``resolved`` / ``query`` are the older forms. ``options``
says which forms and id systems this selection can use (``{key: reason or null}``), and ``captions`` notes
ids that several links share.

A saved selection is resolved again on its network as it is now when that network is open from the same
source (read-only: the current selection is unchanged). ``warnings`` says what the file may not show: a
pin that has gone stale (the links are the ones selected before an edit), or a saved selection that could
not be checked, or was saved on another version.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `what` | query | `fragment` / `projectcard` | no | `"fragment"` |
| `form` | query | `segment` / `link_list` / `resolved` / `query` | no | `"resolved"` |
| `id_system` | query | `gmns` / `osm` / `gers` | no | `"gmns"` |
| `name` | query | string or null | no |  |

Responses: `200` Successful Response · `422` Validation Error

### Assistant

The natural-language assistant: ask, then approve or reject the draft it proposes.

#### `GET /api/assistant`

The conversation, the pending draft and the status.

Responses: `200` Successful Response

#### `POST /api/assistant/ask`

Answer one question; the model call can take seconds (a local model longer). Busy is 409.

Request body: [`AskBody`](#askbody) (JSON).

Responses: `200` Successful Response · `422` Validation Error

#### `POST /api/assistant/drafts/{draft_id}/approve`

Run the pending draft; 409 when it isn't pending, went stale, or the assistant is busy.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | path | integer | yes |  |

Responses: `200` Successful Response · `422` Validation Error

#### `POST /api/assistant/drafts/{draft_id}/reject`

Discard the pending draft; 409 when it isn't pending.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | path | integer | yes |  |

Responses: `200` Successful Response · `422` Validation Error

#### `POST /api/assistant/clear`

Forget the conversation and any pending draft.

Responses: `200` Successful Response

### Language models

| Parameter | In | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | path | string | yes |  |

An authenticated, token-free call to ``provider``; failures are reported in the result.

### Request schemas

#### `AskBody`

One question.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes |  |  |

#### `DeletePlanQuery`

The keys a deletion would start from.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array of integer or string | yes |  |  |

#### `LocateQuery`

Where the row whose primary key is ``id`` sits, in a `RowsQuery`'s order.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` |  |
| `sort` | string or null | no |  |  |
| `dir` | `asc` / `desc` | no | `"asc"` |  |
| `filter` | array of object or null | no |  |  |
| `ids` | array of integer or string or null | no |  |  |
| `related` | [`RelatedQuery`](#relatedquery) or null | no |  |  |
| `related_mode` | `tint` / `filter` | no | `"tint"` |  |
| `tint` | [`RelatedQuery`](#relatedquery) or null | no |  |  |
| `id` | integer or string | yes |  |  |

#### `RelatedQuery`

What to find related records for: highlighted ids per table, and how many keys away.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sources` | object | yes |  |  |
| `hops` | integer | no | `1` |  |

#### `RowsQuery`

One page of a table: the GET parameters as JSON, plus related records to filter by and/or tint.

``related`` with ``related_mode="filter"`` narrows the rows; with ``"tint"`` it only marks them.
``tint`` marks rows by a second set of sources while ``related`` filters (e.g. the selection's lanes,
tinted by what is focused).

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` |  |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` |  |
| `sort` | string or null | no |  |  |
| `dir` | `asc` / `desc` | no | `"asc"` |  |
| `filter` | array of object or null | no |  |  |
| `ids` | array of integer or string or null | no |  |  |
| `related` | [`RelatedQuery`](#relatedquery) or null | no |  |  |
| `related_mode` | `tint` / `filter` | no | `"tint"` |  |
| `tint` | [`RelatedQuery`](#relatedquery) or null | no |  |  |
{% endraw %}

## Examples

Read the session state, apply a no-argument Action, and watch one event from the stream. The
server must be running (`netstead app`) on its default port.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8850/api/state
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8850/api/actions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"type": "clear_selection"}'
curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:8850/api/events?max_events=1'
```

- [Workbench Actions](workbench-actions.md) — the Action schemas `POST /api/actions` accepts.
- [Explore in the Workbench](../cookbook/workbench.md) — the app this API serves.
- [Write a Workbench plugin](../cookbook/workbench-plugins.md) — adding routes under `/api/plugins/<id>/`.
- [Settings reference](settings.md) — `app.host`, `app.port` and `io.allowed_roots`.

summary: Complete reference for the seven MCP tools the netstead server exposes — three generic corral tools plus four GMNS-aware ones.

# MCP tools reference

## Summary

`netstead mcp serve` runs a stdio MCP server that exposes seven tools: three generic Frictionless-package tools inherited from `corral.mcp` (`describe_package`, `validate_package`, `list_tables`), plus four GMNS-aware tools (`describe_network`, `quality_check`, `connected_components`, `scope_from_nodes`). Every tool is **stateless** — each call takes a `source` (path or URL) and loads the package fresh. No session, no cache, no cross-call mutation. A stateful surface (editing sessions, indexed scope ops) is deferred.

All tools return JSON-shaped dicts (or, for `list_tables`, a list of strings); shapes are stable inside a major version. The example outputs below are what the tools return for the bundled Leavenworth fixture (`packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv`: 339 links, 121 nodes, nine CSV tables, no `datapackage.json`). For wiring the server into Claude Desktop or Claude Code, see [Wire the MCP server](../cookbook/serve-mcp.md).

## Tools

### `describe_package(source)`

Generic package overview. Available on any Frictionless package, not just GMNS. It loads the source as a bare `corral.dataset.Package`, so on a CSV directory without a `datapackage.json` the inferred package `name` is `"auto"`; `describe_network` is the GMNS-aware variant.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | Filesystem path or URL to a package directory / `datapackage.json` |

**Returns** — `dict`:

```json
{
  "source": "<echoed input>",
  "name": "auto",
  "engine": "IbisEngine",
  "table_count": 9,
  "tables": [
    {"name": "geometry", "rows": 339, "columns": ["geometry_id", "geometry"]},
    {"name": "lane", "rows": 429, "columns": ["lane_id", "link_id", "lane_num", "allowed_uses", "width"]},
    {"name": "link", "rows": 339, "columns": ["link_id", "name", "from_node_id", "to_node_id", "..."]},
    {"name": "node", "rows": 121, "columns": ["node_id", "name", "x_coord", "y_coord", "node_type", "ctrl_type", "osm_node_id"]}
  ]
}
```

`rows` / `columns` may be `null` for an individual table if its count fails (e.g. unreadable file).

**Example**

```json
{"name": "describe_package", "arguments": {"source": "packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv"}}
```

### `validate_package(source)`

Run corral's **generic** validation pipeline (structural + schema + foreign-key + sync-state) against whatever spec the source carries, and return the report. It does **not** apply the GMNS spec: on a bare CSV directory such as the Leavenworth fixture there is no spec to check against, so `spec_version` is `null` and the findings are one `structural.spec_missing` info (no `datapackage.json`, no spec given) and nine `structural.unexpected_resource` warnings (one per CSV the empty spec does not declare). For GMNS validation use `netstead validate <source> --json`, which emits the same report shape with the vendored spec applied.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | Path or URL to the package |

**Returns** — `dict`, the canonical `ValidationReport.to_dict()` shape:

```json
{
  "report_version": 1,
  "spec_version": null,
  "source": "<echoed input>",
  "created_at": "2026-10-19T13:12:08.078865",
  "metadata": {},
  "summary": {"error": 0, "warning": 9, "info": 1, "data_quality": 0, "is_clean": false},
  "issues": [
    {
      "severity": "info",
      "category": "structural",
      "code": "structural.spec_missing",
      "message": "package source '...': no spec was given and none was found beside the source, so no table was checked against a schema",
      "table": null,
      "column": null,
      "row": null,
      "fix_hint": "Pass spec= to Package.from_source. Only a datapackage.json inside a source directory is discovered automatically; one inside a zip, next to a single file, or at a remote prefix is not.",
      "extra": {}
    },
    {
      "severity": "warning",
      "category": "structural",
      "code": "structural.unexpected_resource",
      "message": "package source '...': resource 'geometry' was found but is not declared in the spec",
      "table": "geometry",
      "column": null,
      "row": null,
      "fix_hint": "Add geometry to the spec, rename it to match an existing declared resource, or remove it from the source.",
      "extra": {"path": ".../geometry.csv", "format": "csv"}
    }
  ]
}
```

`severity` is one of `error`, `warning`, `info`; `category` is one of `schema`, `structural`, `foreign_key`, `sync_state`, `data_quality`. `summary.is_clean` is `true` when there are no `error` or `warning` issues; `info` issues do not affect it. The example above shows the `spec_missing` info and the first of the nine warnings.

**Example**

```json
{"name": "validate_package", "arguments": {"source": "s3://my-bucket/regional/datapackage.json"}}
```

### `list_tables(source)`

Cheap variant of `describe_package` — returns just the sorted list of table names with no row counts. Useful as a first call when the agent doesn't know what's in a package.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | Path or URL |

**Returns** — `list[str]`:

```json
["geometry", "lane", "link", "link_tod", "node", "signal_controller", "time_set_definitions", "use_definition", "use_group"]
```

**Example**

```json
{"name": "list_tables", "arguments": {"source": "packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv"}}
```

### `describe_network(source)`

GMNS-aware version of `describe_package`. Loads the source as a `netstead.Network` (so the GMNS spec is applied and `name` is `"gmns"`) and surfaces the fields an agent typically wants up front — spec version, link/node counts — without iterating tables.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | Path or URL to a GMNS network |

**Returns** — `dict`:

```json
{
  "source": "<echoed input>",
  "name": "gmns",
  "spec_version": "0.97",
  "engine": "IbisEngine",
  "links": 339,
  "nodes": 121,
  "table_count": 9,
  "tables": ["geometry", "lane", "link", "link_tod", "node", "signal_controller", "time_set_definitions", "use_definition", "use_group"]
}
```

`links` / `nodes` may be `null` if the network doesn't have those tables or the count fails.

**Example**

```json
{"name": "describe_network", "arguments": {"source": "packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv"}}
```

### `quality_check(source)`

Run the GMNS data-quality rule pack (high-speed-residential, disconnected components, lane-count mismatch, duplicate-near-nodes, sharp-angle bends, implausible v/c, missing critical fields). Requires the `[graph]` extra (scipy) on the server side for the connectivity rule.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | Path or URL to a GMNS network |

**Returns** — same `ValidationReport.to_dict()` shape as `validate_package`. The report's own `spec_version` and `source` are `null` (the rule runner does not fill them in); every issue has `category: "data_quality"`:

```json
{
  "report_version": 1,
  "spec_version": null,
  "source": null,
  "created_at": "2026-10-19T13:12:08.141843",
  "metadata": {},
  "summary": {"error": 0, "warning": 271, "info": 0, "data_quality": 271, "is_clean": false},
  "issues": [
    {
      "severity": "warning",
      "category": "data_quality",
      "code": "quality.high_speed_residential",
      "message": "link row 0 (link_id=1): facility_type='residential' with free_speed=40.0 > threshold 35.0.",
      "table": "link",
      "column": "free_speed",
      "row": 0,
      "fix_hint": "If the speed is correct, change facility_type to a higher class (e.g. 'tertiary', 'secondary').",
      "extra": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

Default-pack issues are WARNING / INFO — the GMNS spec is silent on these checks, but they catch common data-quality misses. Customize thresholds via the Python API ([Customize the data-quality rule pack](../cookbook/customize-quality.md)).

**Example**

```json
{"name": "quality_check", "arguments": {"source": "packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv"}}
```

### `connected_components(source)`

Count weakly-connected components in the network graph. Requires the `[graph]` extra (scipy) on the server side.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | Path or URL to a GMNS network |

**Returns** — `dict`:

```json
{
  "source": "<echoed input>",
  "component_count": 1,
  "sizes": [121]
}
```

`component_count == 1` means the network is fully connected. `sizes` is the descending list of node counts per component — `[121]` for the fully-connected 121-node Leavenworth fixture; `[60, 12, 3]` for a three-component network whose largest piece has 60 nodes.

**Example**

```json
{"name": "connected_components", "arguments": {"source": "packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv"}}
```

### `scope_from_nodes(source, node_ids, path_between)`

Build a network-aware scope from a list of seed node ids and return the resulting node + link sets.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | — | Path or URL to a GMNS network |
| `node_ids` | list[int] | — | Seed node ids |
| `path_between` | bool | `true` | If true, includes all nodes/links on shortest paths between every pair of seeds. If false, the docstring promises the seeds plus their incident links, but today the scope holds only the seed nodes and no links (seeds `[1, 25, 50]` on Leavenworth give 3 nodes, 0 links, although 20 links touch them). |

**Returns** — `dict` (intended; see the known issue). For seeds `[1, 25, 50]` on Leavenworth the scope has 14 nodes and 28 links:

```json
{
  "source": "<echoed input>",
  "seed_node_ids": [1, 25, 50],
  "path_between": true,
  "result_node_count": 14,
  "result_link_count": 28,
  "node_ids": [1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 15, 25, 50, 63, 74, 78, 96, 99, 100],
  "link_ids": [1, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 27, 29, "..."]
}
```

The returned ids are sorted. For chaining (union / intersect / buffer), drop into the Python API — the MCP surface only exposes the leaf operation.

**Example**

```json
{"name": "scope_from_nodes", "arguments": {"source": "packages/netstead/netstead/fixtures/leavenworth/csv", "node_ids": [1, 25, 50], "path_between": true}}
```
